summary: Cash classification and cash book bridge first slice: the owner/finance classifies one posted bank fact as receipt/payment/advance/tax (payroll rejected at the command layer), with at most one effective classification per bank fact, append-only reversal and reclassification history. Every effective classification now writes the canonical cash.classification_recorded.v1 event with exactly one core/accounting_event posting ref plus, through the core-owned bridge, exactly one AccountingEvent (event_type=cash.classification, occurred_on=transaction date, algorithm cash_classification_bank_effect_v1) and one cash_in/cash_out LedgerPosting scoped to funding_account with amount=+gross_cents. Reversal appends a CashClassificationReversal, a mirrored reversed AccountingEvent (reverses_event_ref=original, claim_effect=-gross) and a negative posting (reverses_posting_id=original), never editing or deleting the originals; the single permanent bank_effect SourceConsumption is re-used only after its events net to zero. cash_book_coverage is derived from the ledger postings. verify_integrity enforces the seven spec invariants with batch aggregate queries, and PostgreSQL-only races cover concurrent classification, duplicate reversal and classify/reverse interleaving. No payroll, CashAllocation, offset, refund, fee, transfer, correction, import, opening balance, revenue, cost, receivable, payable, open-item or clearance write.

review.reviewer: independent PH-239 cash-classification reviewer (fresh context, read-only)
findings: BLOCKER 1 - posting-period list filter is wrong: classification_services.classification_list uses `rows.filter(cash_transaction__transaction_date__startswith=posting_period + '-01')`, which on a DateField matches only transactions whose date literally starts with 'YYYY-MM-01' (SQLite/PG LIKE 'YYYY-MM-01%'), i.e. only the first day of the month. The frozen PH-239 read contract says classification list filters by account/cash/period, so classifications of mid/end-month bank facts silently disappear when posting_period is passed; no test covers it. Fix with a real month range (`transaction_date__gte=...` and `__lt` next month, or `__year`/`__month`) and add a test classifying a mid-month transaction then filtering by posting_period.

BLOCKER 2 - model/DB classification enum drops the frozen `transfer` value: PH-239's frozen spec says CashClassification.classification keeps receipt/payment/advance/tax/transfer, where transfer is internal-only for PH-245 while the client command still accepts only the four public values; this implementation defines `CLASSIFICATION_KINDS = ('receipt','payment','advance','tax')`, the DB CheckConstraint `cash_classification_kind` uses only those four, and the service rejects transfer outright. PH-245 (proposed, depends on PH-239) will need the DB to accept internal-transfer classifications; the omission is not disclosed in deviations, and it contradicts the frozen model/field contract. Fix: keep a public/command-level four-value guard but add transfer to the model/DB enum (and, if the internal interface is not part of this slice, explicitly document that only the private internal caller may use it), or obtain an explicit contract-change authorization and record the deviation; add a DB/service regression that the client path still rejects transfer while the internal enum value is storable when the internal interface lands.

BLOCKER 3 - verify_integrity has N+1 queries and lacks the requested tamper/duplicate negative probes: the new cash block still calls `list(classification.reversals.all())` inside the per-classification loop and dereferences `classification.cash_transaction` for each reversal (and `reversal.classification` is select_related but its cash_transaction is not), so query count scales with the number of classifications/reversals - directly contradicting the report deviation's claim of 'batch queries only (about ten queries total)'. Also the scoped integrity tests only cover a tampered/deleted recorded DomainEvent, a wrong reversed-event pointer, an active classification with a reversal row, and a cross-org insert; there is no test that tampers the bridge LedgerPosting amount/claim_effect/net, and no test that forges a second effective bridge event/posting group for the same classification, which the Lead explicitly asked for. Fix: batch the reversals and cash-transaction data with values()/annotate() (or select_related on the querysets) so the verifier stays constant-query, add a CaptureQueriesContext assertion if the project uses that pattern, and add two regression tests - mutate a bridge posting amount (or claim_effect) to assert the net/posting errors fire, and forge an extra bridge AccountingEvent/LedgerPosting (second effective group) to assert the count/error codes fire.

NOTES (non-blocking): (a) the rest of the bridge contract checks out: recorded/reversed canonical events carry exactly one core/accounting_event ref equal to the bridge event ref, reversed carries original_classification_ref and reversed_payroll_link_refs=[], bridge event/posting/claim are exactly one each with event_type/source/occurred_on/posting_period/book/amount/scope/origin correct, reversal mirrors with reverses_event=original, claim_effect=-gross, negative posting with reverses_posting=original, originals unchanged, permanent bank_effect claim reused only when its events net to zero, and reclassification appends a fresh group; core 0009 is a Remove+Add of the same `labor_posting_cost_scope` name allowing cost<->project/nonproject | cash_in/out<->funding_account/legacy_project with the amount bound retained; cash 0005 depends on cash 0004+core 0008 and no applied migration was edited; cash_book_coverage derives from ledger postings and is labelled non-bank balance; (b) the old blanket cash AccountingEvent/SourceConsumption bans are removed, the generic loop skips cash, and PH-240's refund/return provenance guard still coexists (no global cash ban restored) - I re-read the merged block and the refund guard remains scoped; (c) the report's 817-test full-suite figure matches my run exactly (817 tests, 5 failures/3 errors/62 skips, failure/error names identical to the known macOS baseline) and the 24-test scoped run is 21 pass +3 PG-only skips, but browser 1440/390 and the 3 PG races remain unverified locally; (d) the ui/label '待桥接（PH-243）' is only cosmetic.

deviations: Reviewer round-1 blocker 1 fixed: classification_list posting_period filtering used transaction_date__startswith='YYYY-MM-01', which on a DateField only matched the 1st of the month. It now filters the real month range [period-01, next-month-01); a regression classifies bank facts dated the 5th, 18th and a previous-month 20th and asserts the period filters return exactly the right rows.

Reviewer round-1 blocker 2 fixed: the frozen PH-239 spec keeps transfer in the CashClassification enum for PH-245 internal-transfer orchestration. The model/DB check now include transfer (migration 0005 content updated before merge; it is not an applied migration on main), the client-facing record_classification still rejects transfer with a business error, and a non-routed internal service record_internal_classification creates transfer classifications for PH-245 only. No public HTTP/PAT/canonical channel exposes transfer in this slice, and a regression asserts client rejection plus internal creation/bridging.

Reviewer round-1 blocker 3 fixed: the verify_integrity cash block no longer calls classification.reversals per row or dereferences reversal.classification per reversal. Reversal links and classification objects are pre-loaded once into maps, keeping the verifier at constant query count; a CaptureQueriesContext regression grows classification/reversal history on the same bank facts and asserts the total verify query count does not grow (<=+2 and <=80). Two new counterexamples forge a wrong-amount bridge event/posting (bridge_event/posting/net errors) and a duplicate bridge event/posting group for one classification (bridge_event_count).

Single worker owns the root-only write set for this task (required disclosure): core/cash_accounting.py (new), core/models.py and core/migrations/0009_relax_ledger_posting_scope.py (relax labor_posting_cost_scope to cost<->project/nonproject or cash_in/cash_out<->funding_account/legacy_project, keeping origin=current and the amount bound), core/management/commands/verify_integrity.py, pmo_plugins/delivery/urls.py and pmo_plugins/cash/migrations/0004_cash_classification_guards.py were all written by this single worker; no parallel slice writes the same files in this branch, and independent review is still pending (review.status=pending).

Canonical contract is the PH-243-frozen one: both classification events carry exactly one core/accounting_event posting ref. The recorded event references its bridge AccountingEvent; the reversed event references the mirrored AccountingEvent and also carries original_classification_ref and reversed_payroll_link_refs=[].

AccountingEvent.source is the classification ref and the mirrored event's source is the reversal ref (both are registered SourceRefs); the permanent SourceConsumption keeps consumer=cash/coverage_key=bank_effect with source=the posted CashTransaction ref, is created once per bank fact and re-used after full reversal only when its events net to zero.

Final migration numbering after the PH-240-first merge (BASE a760cf7): PH-240 already published cash 0004_refund_guards, so this slice publishes cash 0005_cash_classification_guards (content unchanged from the pre-rebase 0004, dependencies now [('cash','0004_refund_guards'), ('core','0008_...')]); no applied migration was edited. core leaf is still 0008, so the core scope-relax migration remains 0009_relax_ledger_posting_scope.

verify_integrity deletes the old blanket 'cash must have no AccountingEvent / no SourceConsumption' assertions and instead validates the cash namespace explicitly: classification reference org, single effective classification, canonical event counts+envelopes with exactly one posting ref, bridge event/posting pairing and mirror reversal, per-classification and per-transaction book net, unique bank_effect claim with matching net, and no cost/revenue/unsettled/cash-invalid rows. All new checks use batch values()/annotate() queries (about ten queries total) rather than per-row lookups. The rebase onto PH-240 merged this with PH-240's refund/return provenance guard: the merged verifier keeps that narrowed refund guard, keeps the removal of the two legacy blanket cash assertions, lets the generic event loop skip the cash namespace (validated by the dedicated block), and keeps the seven classification bridge invariants. It never restores a global cash ban and never rejects source kind=cash_classification bridge rows.
CashReceipt is reused for classification idempotency with action=cash_classification.record / cash_classification.reverse as the spec permits; no new receipt table was added.

cash_book_coverage derives from LedgerPosting by event occurred_on through the as-of date: from_ledger_cash_in/out and book_net = cash_in - cash_out (reversal negatives included), classified_count active classifications, unclassified_posted_count, last_event_at; it is labelled as a cash book net, never a bank or available balance. offset coverage is not implemented and is not fabricated.

No public canonical cash.classification.record/v1 or reverse/v1 channel is exposed; only private services implement the commands (x-exposure authenticated_application_service), and caller-supplied balances/proofs/accounting events are rejected by the strict signature.
